arch_sec2_gcpsg004: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP Lead Security Agency, GCPSG-004 (2020) Security Lighting Considerations Guide, effective 2020-12-02 (the page's effective-date line names another guide): 7.2 CCVE surveillance zones 'Average light level should be at least 20 lux. Minimum 0.33 uniformity ratio. Measured vertically from 1.5m off the ground'; patrolled/sensored perimeters 'average light level of 20 lux from 3m on the patrol side to 9m on the approach side', 'Tight beam control should be used to limit light spill onto neighboring properties and roads'; staff entrances '50-200 lux using wall mounted luminaires 3-4m above ground level'; paths 20 lux, 5 lux at 5 m; open parking 25 lux, enclosed 65 lux; sally ports 100 lux; luminaires 'above and behind security cameras'; 7.1 backlight less than four times front light; 8 switch on below 40 lux; 6.4 CRI 80+ — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-004-2020-security-lighting-considerations-guide
arch_sec2_gcpsg009b: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-009 (2022) Security Fencing Considerations Guide (official RCMP page; supplements register rcmpGCPSG009): 9.1 outer setback 'often cleared and trimmed', 'Inner setbacks should be kept clear of any obstructions', no widths; 9.6 fence disturbance and deflection (taut wire) detection, 'Detection is more reliable when combining more than one type of sensing technology'; 10.1 video surveillance alone 'is not an effective method of detection'; 10.2 double fences 'The recommended spacing is at least twice the fence height'; 10.6 'Gates are typically the weakest portion of any fence'; 10.7 LED fence lighting, 'Aim towards the unsecured side'; 10.10 compacted gravel 300 mm deep 'extending at least 900mm on either side' — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-009-2022-security-fencing-considerations-guide
arch_sec2_gcpsg011b: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-011 (2024) Guide to CCTV/CCVE Systems (supplements arch_acc_gcpsg011): 7.3.2 cameras 'capable of capturing/viewing the entire space intended' where no overlap; 'Mounting CCTV cameras in ceiling corners, on top of building structures, or on top of security lighting poles'; 7.1.1 fixed cameras 'Commonly used for 24/7 monitoring of perimeter fencing and open spaces'; 5.1.2 blind spots and poor coverage as detection limits; 6.2.1 lighting per GCPSG-004, assess at night; 6.1 signage set by the AHJ; no mounting heights, lux or pixel-density figures — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-011-2024-guide-closed-circuit-televisionclosed-circuit-video-equipment-systems
arch_sec2_gcpsg014b: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-014 (2024) Physical Security Considerations in Facility Design (supplements arch_sec_gcpsg014): 6.2 avoid 'Incentives for unauthorized personnel to cross zoning boundaries' (e.g. washrooms, cafeterias); 6.9 'security and safety glazing included in the design phase', per GCPSG-013; 6.12 air intakes, ducts, roof hatches safeguarded, 'Utility spaces should not be located adjacent to entrances to more restrictive zones'; 6.13 'The impact of departmental operations on adjacent occupants should be considered'; 7.1.1.1 'Fencing should be used for the perimeter of the site'; 7.1.1.2 general illumination per GCPSG-004; 7.1.1.3 'clear lines of sight at eye level to and from the building'; 7.1.1.4 'The building and the site should be observable from the roadway by first responders and passers-by' unless a TRA says otherwise — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-014-2024-physical-security-considerations-facility-design
arch_sec2_gcpsg021: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-021 (2025) Fundamentals of Detection Systems in Physical Security, effective 2025-04-25: 'Vibration detectors are most commonly installed on fences'; 'A perimeter fence is the most common first layer of defense'; 'CCTV systems can be programed to begin recording an area anytime a detection device is triggered'; contact sensors 'most commonly employed on doors and windows'; Table 2 Operations Zone 'Restrict surveillance to access points and travel routes'; no clear-zone widths, buried, microwave or IR systems — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/gcpsg-021-2025-fundamentals-detection-systems-physical-security
arch_sec2_gcpsg003: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP, GCPSG-003 (2021) Security Operations Centre Design Considerations Guide, effective 2021-08-09: 4.3 'Typically, the SOC should be out of sight but within audible range of the public'; 6.6 'The SOC should be designated as a Security Zone and be nested within an Operations Zone'; item 5 'protected on all six sides from brute force entry attack'; item 8 brute-force doors and frames; item 9 interlocked vestibule; item 2 video 'clear enough to identify all individuals entering through portals into each respective space', 'should not view the interior of the space'; 6.3 SPC 85 for the control room; 6.4 wheelchair clearances 1200 x 900 mm; 7-14 equipment room adjacent, 1.5 m round racks, 50% spare capacity; no room area figures — https://rcmp.ca/en/lead-security-agency-physical-security/guidance-and-publications/gcpsg-003-2021-security-operations-centre-design-considerations-guide
arch_sec2_g1302: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: RCMP Lead Agency Publication G13-02, Secure Demising Wall, 2013-01-15 (named by GCPSG-015 App. C 2.3 for a secure data centre perimeter): p. 7 slab-to-slab, wood or steel-frame floors and roofs reinforced to match, no pass-throughs in the critical attack area; p. 10 2" x 6" 18 ga studs at 300 mm oc, welded or riveted 'not screws'; p. 11 expanded metal mesh EMMA 557-99 Style 3/4-9F (0.120" strand) or 16 ga sheet steel on the attack side; 'Screws ... are NOT acceptable'; p. 12 3/16" rivets at 200 mm oc; p. 13 16 ga sheet steel inside the room extending 1200 mm from the door edge; p. 6 two layers 16 mm fire-rated gypsum, 150 mm batts; p. 8 doors and windows 'moderate resistance to force attacks' — https://rcmp.ca/sites/default/files/doc/g13-02-eng.pdf

arch_sec2_fm115: INSURER GUIDE: FM Property Loss Prevention Data Sheet 1-15, Roof-Mounted Solar Photovoltaic Panels, April 2026 (full revision): 1.0 roof PV only; 'See ... Data Sheet 1-57, Plastics in Construction, for wall-mounted, building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) façade systems'; 2.0 an FM Approved Class 1A roof has the rating 'negated once PV panels are placed above it' unless the system is FM Approved; 2.1.1.4 A 'Use only noncombustible frames and mounting systems'; B arrays max 150 x 150 ft (46 x 46 m); C min 4 ft (1.2 m) aisle to next array; D 4 ft to expansion joints; E 6 ft to skylights; 3.2 encapsulants, backsheets and adhesives 'can ignite' — https://www.fm.com/-/media/project/publicwebsites/fmglobal/documentum-new/data-sheet-individual/01-construction/fmds0115.pdf
arch_sec2_fmBipv2025: INSURER RESEARCH: G. Agarwal, 'Fire Performance Evaluation of Building Integrated Photovoltaic (BIPV) Façade Systems', FM technical report, Nov 2025 (project RW000606), ANSI/FM 4411 16-ft parallel panel test: three of four double-sided glass cavity-wall BIPV exceeded peak HRR thresholds with fire to the top; the 6 mm glass system ~780 kW, fire confined to ~8 ft; flexible BIPV ~11 MW, flames >30 ft (9.1 m); EN 13501-1 and UL 1703 accreditation did not correlate with façade performance; proposed FM 4483 criteria peak HRR <=830 kW (unlimited height) (read from executive summary; text truncated after 7.1.2) — https://www.fm.com/-/media/project/publicwebsites/fm/files/resources/research-technical-reports/2025_agarwal_bipv_fire_performance_evaluation_public_release_format_final.pdf
arch_sec2_axaPrc205: INSURER GUIDE: AXA XL Risk Consulting, PRC.2.0.5 Protection of Buildings from Exterior Fire Exposures, (c) 2020: separation per NFPA 80A guide numbers, (guide number x height) + 5 ft (1.5 m); example 100 ft x 25 ft wall, 25% openings, severe, guide no. 2.55 -> 68.75 ft (21 m); within half the distance a blank 3 h wall; openings within 5 ft (1.5 m) filled or 3 h shutters, within 10 ft (3 m) 1 1/2 h, within half the distance 3/4 h; beyond half wired glass and deluge water curtain; lower-roof table not needed if exposing roof is concrete or >=1 h (some text garbled in extraction) — https://qac-cms.axaxl.com/-/media/axaxl/files/pdfs/prc-guidelines/prc-2/prc205protectionofbuildingsfromexteriorfireexposuresv1.pdf
arch_sec2_opS710: INSURER GUIDE (EU): OP Insurance Ltd / A-Insurance Ltd (Finland), Safety Regulation S710 'Data centres', valid from 1 Jan 2018: 4.2 'Any unmanned data centre should be located in the middle of a building in a windowless room'; 'It must not be possible to remove the construction or any part of it from the outside without breaking it'; 'A Class 3 anti-burglar wall'; high-protection centres need an insurer-approved crime detection system, at least Class 3 (SFS-EN 50131-1), to a 24 h manned centre, duplicated transmission, anti-mask detectors, local sirens inside and outside; 4.4/4.9 ventilation plant and standby power in separate fire compartments; 4.5 consider toilets, heating water, roof above the hall; above ground floor or raised — https://www.op.fi/documents/20556/65462/Data+centres+S710/e7c01200-baf9-44ef-b89a-db06a715cf8c

arch_sec2_nbc3155: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 3.1.5.4–3.1.5.6 (identical text in BCBC 2024, VBBL 2025 and NBC(AE) 2023, repo copies data/raw/codes/): 3.1.5.4.(2) 'Combustible vertical glazing installed no higher than the second storey is permitted in a building required to be of noncombustible construction', FSR <=75 (<=150 if <=25% of wall with conditions); 3.1.5.5.(1) combustible cladding permitted if building 'not more than 3 storeys' or 'sprinklered throughout' and CAN/ULC-S134 wall test: flaming 'does not spread more than 5 m above the opening' and heat flux 'not more than 35 kW/m2 measured at 3.5 m above the opening'; (2) Table 3.2.3.7 governs where limiting distance permits <=10% unprotected openings; (4) Appendix D-6 assemblies deemed to comply; 3.1.5.6 combustible components: same test or 25 mm masonry/concrete cladding; A-3.1.5.5.(1)(b)(ii) 'flame does not spread on the exterior surface ... where the heat flux is less than 35 kW/m2' — local copy of NBC 2020 (NRC)
